Title: Update existing order while retaining existing permanent customer and item photos
Preconditions: An active order exists in the system with a customer photo already stored in permanent storage (URL path containing 'customers') and a measurement group cloth photo stored in permanent storage (URL path containing 'orders').
Steps:
1. Navigate to the Order Update screen for the existing order.
2. Modify non-photo fields such as delivery date or special instructions, keeping the customer photo and cloth photo fields populated with their existing permanent URLs.
3. Save the order changes.

Test Data: orderId: 101, customerPhoto: "http://minio/customer-photos/customers/cust_101.jpg", clothPhoto: "http://minio/order-photos/orders/cloth_101.jpg", deliveryDate: "2026-04-20"
Expected Result: The order updates successfully with HTTP 200 OK. The existing customer photo and item cloth photo URLs remain unchanged, and no temp-to-permanent file relocation is executed.

Title: Update existing order with a newly uploaded customer photo from temporary storage
Preconditions: An existing order is recorded in the system. A new customer photo has been uploaded to temporary storage and has a temporary photo URL (path does not contain 'customers').
Steps:
1. Open the edit screen for the existing order.
2. Replace the customer photo with the newly uploaded temporary photo URL.
3. Submit the updated order.

Test Data: orderId: 101, customerPhoto: "temp-bucket/temp_customer_789.jpg"
Expected Result: The order is updated successfully. The new customer photo is relocated from temporary storage to permanent customer storage, and the updated customer profile displays the new permanent image URL.

Title: Verify that photo processing failure during order update does not leak internal storage details or raw exception messages
Preconditions: An existing order exists in the system
Steps:
1. Send a request to update an existing order containing a new customer photo URL that triggers a storage processing error. 2. Inspect the returned error message in the response.

Test Data: Order ID: 101, customerPhoto: 'temp/invalid-storage-key.jpg'
Expected Result: The system fails the order update and returns a generic error message 'Unable to process customer photo at this time. Please try again later.' without leaking internal MinIO bucket names, server endpoints, or raw stack traces.

Title: Verify order photo uploads prepend configured prefix 'orders/' to object keys in order-photos bucket
Preconditions: Application is deployed with minio.order-photo-prefix=orders/ in application.properties. MinIO service and order-photos bucket are accessible.
Steps:
1. Upload a photo for a new or existing order. 2. Query the object storage or check file metadata via API. 3. Inspect the stored object key in the 'order-photos' bucket.

Test Data: minio.order-photo-prefix=orders/
Expected Result: The uploaded order photo is stored with an object key prefixed with 'orders/' (e.g., 'orders/sample-photo.jpg') in the order-photos bucket.

Title: Verify customer photo uploads prepend configured prefix 'customers/' to object keys in customer-photos bucket
Preconditions: Application is deployed with minio.customer-photo-prefix=customers/ in application.properties. MinIO service and customer-photos bucket are accessible.
Steps:
1. Upload a customer profile or reference photo. 2. Query object storage or check photo path details via API response. 3. Inspect the stored object key in the 'customer-photos' bucket.

Test Data: minio.customer-photo-prefix=customers/
Expected Result: The uploaded customer photo is stored with an object key prefixed with 'customers/' (e.g., 'customers/customer-123.jpg') in the customer-photos bucket.

Title: Verify temporary file cleanup runs on schedule using updated property key 'minio.cleanup-interval-ms'
Preconditions: Application is deployed with updated minio.cleanup-interval-ms=300000 setting. A temp file older than 30 minutes exists in tailor-photos-temp bucket.
Steps:
1. Place a temporary file older than 30 minutes in the 'tailor-photos-temp' bucket. 2. Observe background logs and bucket contents across the 300,000 ms (5 minute) cleanup interval cycle. 3. Check if the expired file is purged.

Test Data: minio.temp-cleanup-interval-ms (old) -> minio.cleanup-interval-ms=300000 (new)
Expected Result: The background cleanup process triggers every 300,000 ms using the new 'minio.cleanup-interval-ms' property key and removes files older than the retention threshold from the tailor-photos-temp bucket without errors.
